title: Coagulation and vitamin K before surgery in obstructive jaundice
logic: If a patient with obstructive jaundice is booked for any operative or drainage procedure and no coagulation profile (or documented vitamin K administration) is recorded in the current episode, the booking is incomplete — obstructed biliary drainage impairs vitamin-K-dependent clotting.
action: Flag the booking; prompt coagulation testing and preoperative vitamin K; require documented senior override for emergencies that cannot wait.

title: Tissue diagnosis attached to every gastric bypass or resection
logic: If a gastrojejunostomy or gastric resection is being recorded and no biopsy of the obstructing or resected lesion is captured (preoperative endoscopic or intraoperative), the operative record is incomplete — benign-appearing outlet obstruction may be malignant.
action: Require a biopsy entry (or explicit documented reason for its absence) before the operative note can be finalised; open a histology-tracking task automatically.

title: Cholangitis triad triggers the biliary sepsis pathway
logic: If a patient presents with fever or rigors plus jaundice plus right upper quadrant pain (Charcot pattern), classify as acute cholangitis; adding hypotension or confusion classifies severe cholangitis.
action: Route to the biliary sepsis pathway: blood cultures, intravenous antibiotics covering biliary flora, and urgent biliary decompression planning (ERCP where available, otherwise surgical); severe cholangitis escalates to EMERGENCY decompression and highest-acuity bed.

title: Suspected cystic neoplasm exits the pseudocyst pathway
logic: If a pancreatic cystic lesion has no antecedent pancreatitis history, or shows septations, mural nodules, or solid components on imaging, it must not be classified as a pseudocyst.
action: Reclassify as indeterminate cystic lesion; block simple internal-drainage listing; route to central hospital MDT for neoplasm work-up.

title: Bilious drain output after gastric or biliary surgery
logic: If drain output after gastrectomy, cholecystectomy, or bile duct surgery becomes bilious, or the patient develops fever, tachycardia, or peritonism in the first postoperative week, a duodenal stump leak or bile leak is presumed until excluded.
action: Raise a danger-sign alert; senior surgical review within 1 hour; nil by mouth and fluid resuscitation; senior decision on imaging, drainage, or return to theatre — do not simply observe a bilious drain.

title: Fever after splenectomy is never trivial
logic: If a post-splenectomy patient (any interval since surgery, lifelong) presents with fever, overwhelming post-splenectomy infection must be presumed; in malaria-endemic settings severe malaria is a parallel presumption.
action: Alert the clinician to treat as sepsis immediately: cultures, empirical broad-spectrum antibiotics without waiting for results, and malaria testing; flag splenectomy status prominently on the patient banner.

title: Biliary and upper GI prophylaxis targets enteric and biliary flora
logic: If a biliary, gastric, or pancreatic procedure is booked, give intravenous cefazolin (or ceftriaxone per local policy for high-risk biliary cases) within 60 minutes before incision, adding metronidazole where the gut lumen will be opened; established cholangitis or perforation converts prophylaxis to a treatment course.
action: Prompt agent, timing, and lumen-opening question at induction; record administration time; suppress prophylaxis prompt when a treatment course is charted.

title: Splenectomy vaccination and education bundle
logic: If a splenectomy is planned electively, vaccination against pneumococcus, meningococcus, and Haemophilus influenzae type b is due at least 2 weeks before surgery; if splenectomy was emergent, the same vaccines are due before discharge, together with documented lifelong infection-risk education.
action: Auto-generate the vaccination task at listing (elective) or at operation coding (emergency); block discharge summary sign-off until vaccination status and education are recorded or explicitly deferred with a follow-up booking.

title: Drain surveillance after HPB and gastric surgery
logic: If a drain is in place after hepatobiliary, pancreatic, or gastric surgery, record volume and character at least daily; bilious, amylase-rich, or feculent change, or abrupt high volume, requires same-day surgical review; drains should have a documented removal plan by day 5.
action: Generate daily drain-charting tasks with character classification; alert the team on any concerning character change; flag any drain without a removal decision by postoperative day 5.

title: Post-gastrectomy long-term follow-up obligations
logic: If a patient has undergone partial or total gastrectomy, they require: histology-driven oncology MDT review within 4 weeks; lifelong vitamin B12 replacement (all total, and monitored after distal gastrectomy); iron and nutritional surveillance annually; and early re-referral for recurrent dysphagia, weight loss, or anaemia.
action: Auto-generate the B12 replacement recurring task and annual nutritional review at discharge coding; route histology to MDT; provide red-flag re-referral criteria on the discharge summary.
